title: Countable saturated models: realizing all finite-parameter types
summary: Construct a countable saturated model exactly when every finite-context type set is countable, and deduce elementary universality and existence of a prime model.
abstract: A type may have a solution in an elementary extension while no element of the original model realizes it. Can we enlarge a countable model enough to solve every type over each finite set of parameters and still keep the model countable? The answer depends on how many complete descriptions the theory allows. We first meet all requests based on the original model, then repeat with the new elements available as parameters. The union is saturated. This construction characterizes the existence of countable saturated and elementary-universal models. The same bound on types also permits the opposite construction: a countable prime model obtained by omitting every nonisolated type.
